question.text: For a Cat III AIF classified as an 'equity-oriented investment fund', a minimum equity allocation of what percentage is required?

answer.text: More than 65% of total proceeds/investible funds in listed equity shares of domestic companies

explanation.text: The Logic: A Category III AIF qualifies as an "equity-oriented investment fund" (in the non-fund-of-fund case) when more than 65% of its total proceeds/investible funds are invested in listed equity shares of domestic companies. The Trap: 30%, 50% and 90% are not the prescribed threshold for the equity-oriented classification in this case. Note: For measurement, the source uses the annual average of monthly opening and closing NAV averages. A separate 90%/90% condition applies when a Category III AIF invests through units of another listed fund.
